name: Cuban Beef Picadillo over Polenta with Red Cabbage, Carrot & Jalapeno Slaw (Two Ways)

instructions.primary_message: This recipe was created to feed two adults and two young children. You know your child (their tastes and appetite) best. Use this recipe as a template, adjusting ingredients, cooking methods, and portions as needed.

In a medium saucepan, bring broth to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, reduce heat to low and gradually add polenta to the pan in a thin steady stream, whisking continuously, until incorporated. Cover and cook, stirring occasionally, until polenta is soft and creamy, 15-20 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
3 cups chicken or vegetable broth
1 cup polenta (cornmeal)

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
While the skillet heats up, peel, halve, and small dice onion; peel and mince garlic.
instructions.secondary_message:
½ medium yellow onion
1 clove garlic

instructions.primary_message: Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add onion, garlic, beef, salt, and pepper; cook, breaking the meat apart with a spoon, until browned and crumbly, 5-7 minutes. Transfer beef to a plate and set aside. (Reserve skillet with drippings for later use.)
instructions.secondary_message:
2 tsp extra virgin olive oil
454 g lean ground beef
½ tsp salt
¼ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 small bunch cilantro
1 jalapeño pepper
½ small head red cabbage

instructions.primary_message: Trim, seed, and medium dice bell peppers.

Return skillet (with drippings) to medium-high heat. Add bell pepper, salt, and pepper; cook, stirring occasionally, until fork-tender, 2-3 minutes. Transfer 1 cup of the cooked bell pepper to another plate, along with 1 cup of the cooked beef, and set aside.
instructions.secondary_message:
⅛ tsp salt
⅛ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Return remaining beef to the skillet with the remaining bell pepper, along with tomatoes, vinegar, and spices. Stir to combine the beef picadillo, then cook, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened, 2-3 minutes.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 (411 g) can diced tomatoes
2 tsp red wine vinegar
½ tsp cumin, ground
½ tsp oregano, dried
⅛ tsp crushed red pepper

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, shave cilantro leaves off the stems; discard stems and mince the leaves. Add half to the skillet with the beef, along with olives, and stir to combine. Remove from heat and cover to keep warm.  (Reserve remaining cilantro for the next step.)
Place remaining cilantro in a medium bowl, along with additional vinegar, maple syrup, and spices, then whisk to combine the dressing.
instructions.secondary_message:
red wine vinegar
2 tsp pure maple syrup
½ tsp oregano, dried
¼ tsp salt
¼ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon to reduce spice level. Small dice and add to the bowl with the dressing. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)

Quarter cabbage lengthwise, then cut out and discard the core; slice crosswise into thin (shred-like) strips. Add to the bowl, along with half of the shredded carrots, and toss to combine the slaw. (Reserve remaining carrots for the kid plates.)

When the polenta is done, add oil, salt, and pepper to the pan, then stir to combine. If the polenta is too firm, add hot water, 1 tablespoon at a time, until you reach a desired consistency. Remove from heat.
instructions.secondary_message:
extra virgin olive oil
¼ tsp salt
¼ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message:
FOR THE KID PLATES: Divide 1 cup of polenta, plain beef, bell peppers, and reserved shredded carrots between plates. 

FOR THE ADULT PLATES: Divide remaining polenta between plates or bowls and top with the beef picadillo. Serve with slaw and enjoy!
